In accordance with Office of Personnel Management policy, federal employees are assumed to have gained experience by performing duties and responsibilities appropriate for their official series and grade level as described in their position description.

Experience that would not normally be part of the employee's position is creditable, however, when documented by satisfactory evidence, such as a signed memorandum from the employee's supervisor or an SF-50 or SF-52 documenting an official detail or other official assignment.

The documentation must indicate whether the duties were performed full time or, if part time, the "percentage of times" the other duties were performed. It is expected that this documentation is included in the employee's official personnel record.

In order to receive credit for experience in your resume that is not within the official series and grade level of your official position, you must provide a copy of the appropriate documentation of such experience as indicated above.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through national Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; community; student; social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to gain employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Project Manager – Large Projects Administrative Project Management Focus Position Summary The Project Manager – Large Projects is responsible for the administrative coordination, governance, documentation, tracking, and reporting required to support large, complex projects.

This role ensures that project information is organized, timelines are visible, actions are tracked, risks and issues are documented, and stakeholders have accurate information to support decision-making. This role does not own solution design, deployment strategy, customer adoption, operational readiness, or business execution.

Instead, the Project Manager provides the structure, cadence, documentation, and administrative discipline needed to keep large projects organized and transparent.

This is an individual contributor role that works closely with project sponsors, workstream owners, Solution Deployment Leaders, commercial teams, operations, finance, legal, quality, supply chain, digital, and other stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities: Project Administration and Coordination Maintain project plans, timelines, milestones, action trackers, decision logs, risk logs, issue logs, and dependency trackers. Coordinate project meetings, governance forums, steering committee reviews, and stakeholder update sessions.

Prepare meeting agendas, capture minutes, document decisions, and follow up on assigned actions. Ensure project documentation is complete, current, organized, and accessible to appropriate stakeholders. Support consistent use of project templates, tools, trackers, and reporting formats.

Governance Support Support project governance by maintaining meeting cadence, escalation records, approval documentation, and decision history. Track required approvals, sign-offs, stage gates, and governance checkpoints. Ensure project sponsors and workstream owners have accurate information for reviews and decisions.

Maintain visibility to open decisions, overdue actions, unresolved issues, and upcoming milestones. Help ensure governance processes are followed consistently across large projects. Timeline and Milestone Tracking Maintain the master project timeline based on input from workstream owners and accountable business leads.

Track progress against milestones, deliverables, and agreed due dates. Identify and flag timeline variances, overdue items, and dependency gaps for review by accountable owners. Consolidate updates from multiple workstreams into a single project view. Support visibility to critical path items without owning execution of the underlying work.

Reporting and Communication Support Prepare project status reports, dashboards, executive summaries, and stakeholder updates. Consolidate inputs from workstream owners, deployment leaders, finance, operations, commercial teams, and other functions.

Ensure project reports clearly reflect status, milestones, risks, issues, decisions needed, and next steps. Maintain accurate records of project communications and leadership updates. Support consistent and timely information flow across project stakeholders. Risk, Issue, and Action Tracking Maintain risk, issue, action, and dependency logs.

Document risk descriptions, issue status, owners, target dates, mitigation updates, and escalation history. Follow up with accountable owners to obtain updates and closure status. Flag overdue actions, unresolved issues, or missing information to project sponsors or designated leads.

Support escalation documentation but does not own resolution of technical, operational, commercial, or deployment issues. Budget and Resource Administration Track project budget information, purchase orders, invoices, resource assumptions, and financial updates as directed by finance or project sponsors.

Consolidate budget and resource inputs for project reporting. Maintain documentation related to project spend, approvals, forecasts, and financial decisions. Support administrative coordination of vendor documentation, contracts, statements of work, and related records.

Flag missing financial information, pending approvals, or budget variances for review by accountable owners. Documentation and Records Management Maintain organized project repositories, files, version control, and document naming standards.

Ensure key project documents, approvals, meeting records, reports, and governance materials are stored appropriately. Support audit readiness by maintaining clear records of decisions, approvals, risks, changes, and status updates. Capture lessons learned and archive project materials at project close.

Support continuous improvement of project administration tools, templates, and documentation practices. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, project management, life sciences, engineering, or related field preferred.

Experience supporting large projects, complex initiatives, project management offices, commercial operations, business operations, or administrative project coordination. Strong skills in project documentation, meeting coordination, status reporting, action tracking, and records management.

Ability to consolidate information from multiple stakeholders into clear, accurate project updates. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple deadlines, documents, trackers, and reporting cycles. Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Proficiency with project management, collaboration, reporting, and productivity tools. Ability to work in a matrixed organization and follow up with stakeholders across functions and levels. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting large customer, commercial, operational, supply chain, digital, or transformation projects.

Experience in life sciences, pharmaceutical, biopharma, healthcare, diagnostics, laboratory, manufacturing, or regulated environments. Familiarity with project governance, PMO practices, stage-gate processes, and executive reporting.

Experience with tools such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams, Power BI, CRM, ERP, or similar platforms. Understanding of budget tracking, purchase order processes, vendor documentation, or contract administration. Project management certification or training preferred but not required.

Key Competencies Project administration Documentation management Meeting coordination Status reporting Timeline tracking Action-item follow-up Risk and issue logging Governance support Records management Attention to detail Stakeholder follow-up Tool and tracker discipline Scope and Impact The Project Manager – Large Projects is an individual contributor role focused on the administrative management of large, complex projects.

The role supports project transparency, governance discipline, documentation quality, leadership visibility, and timely follow-up. The role does not own solution deployment, customer adoption, operational readiness, business execution, technical solution design, or commercial strategy.

Accountability for those activities remains with designated business owners, Solution Deployment Leaders, Solution Architects, commercial leaders, and functional teams. Gebäudeautomation ist für Sie mehr als ein Schaltschrank mit Blinklicht? Sie verstehen, wie MSR-Technik, DDC, Inbetriebnahme, Schnittstellen und Bauablauf zusammenhängen – und möchten Verantwortung für Projekte übernehmen, bei denen Technik wirklich wirken muss?
Für ein etabliertes mittelständisches Unternehmen aus der Technischen Gebäudeausrüstung suchen wir im Rahmen der Direktvermittlung eine erfahrene Persönlichkeit für den Bereich MSR und Gebäudeautomation. Das Unternehmen plant und realisiert technische Gebäudesysteme über mehrere Gewerke hinweg und verbindet Elektrotechnik, HLS, MSR und Projektumsetzung in einem praxisnahen Umfeld.
Diese Position ist ideal für Menschen, die Gebäudeautomation nicht nur theoretisch kennen, sondern auch im Projektalltag, auf der Baustelle und in der Abstimmung mit Kunden, Technikern und Nachunternehmern sicher bewegen können.
Aufgaben
Sie übernehmen Verantwortung für laufende Bauvorhaben im Bereich MSR und Gebäudeautomation. Dabei steuern und koordinieren Sie Mitarbeitende, Nachunternehmer, Material und Abläufe und sorgen dafür, dass Qualität, Termine und Ergebnisse zusammenpassen.
Sie unterstützen fachlich bei DDC-Programmierungen, Inbetriebnahmen und Dokumentationen und behalten gleichzeitig die administrative Seite der Projekte im Blick. Dazu gehören technische Planung, Kalkulation, Rechnungslegung, Nachtragsmanagement und die Überwachung der Baustellenergebnisse.
Sie arbeiten eng mit angrenzenden Bereichen der Anlagentechnik zusammen, stimmen Bauabläufe ab und sind Ansprechpartner für interne und externe Projektbeteiligte. Auch Kundenkontakt und die Weiterentwicklung der Abteilung können Teil Ihrer Rolle sein.
Kurz gesagt: Sie verbinden Technik, Organisation und Führung in einem Bereich, der für moderne Gebäude immer wichtiger wird.
Qualifikation
Sie haben ein Studium der Elektrotechnik, Automatisierungstechnik oder eine technische Ausbildung mit Weiterbildung zum Meister oder Techniker abgeschlossen.
Wichtig sind Erfahrung in MSR-Technik, Gebäudeautomation, DDC, GLT oder vergleichbaren Systemen sowie ein gutes Verständnis für Bauabläufe und Projektsteuerung. Kenntnisse gängiger Normen, technischer Vorschriften und Kalkulationsgrundlagen sind hilfreich.
Erfahrung mit bestimmten Systemherstellern ist ein Vorteil, aber entscheidend ist nicht nur ein einzelnes Fabrikat. Wichtiger ist, dass Sie Gebäudeautomation grundsätzlich verstehen, technische Zusammenhänge erklären können und im Projektalltag strukturiert, kostenbewusst und lösungsorientiert handeln.
Sie sollten sicher auftreten, klar kommunizieren und Freude daran haben, technische Teams, Kunden und Projektbeteiligte zusammenzuführen.

Geboten werden eine attraktive Vergütung, 30 Urlaubstage, jährliche Sonderzahlungen abhängig von Leistung und Unternehmenserfolg, eine strukturierte Einarbeitung sowie ein Dienstfahrzeug. Die private Nutzung kann individuell besprochen werden.
Weiterbildungen werden finanziell und zeitlich unterstützt. Zusätzlich bietet das Unternehmen betriebliche Altersvorsorge, kurze Entscheidungswege und ein Umfeld, in dem MSR und Gebäudeautomation nicht als Randthema laufen, sondern als wichtiger Bestandteil moderner technischer Gebäudeausrüstung.
Dann freuen wir uns auf Ihre Bewerbung oder eine unverbindliche Kontaktaufnahme. Auch wenn Sie bisher eher aus der Inbetriebnahme, Systemtechnik oder Projekttechnik kommen und sich in Richtung Bauleitung oder Projektverantwortung entwickeln möchten, lohnt sich ein Gespräch.

s.h: A taste of what you’ll do
s.t:
The Technical Project Manager is responsible for leading complex, high-impact projects and programs that span multiple departments, regions, or product lines. This role combines strategic leadership, technical expertise, and operational excellence to deliver projects that drive organizational growth and innovation.
The Technical Project Manager ensures alignment between business strategy and project execution, mentors mid-level PMs, and influences key stakeholders across technical, operational, and executive levels. This role is central to fostering project management excellence, implementing advanced methodologies, and leveraging technology — including AI-enabled tools — to improve delivery and decision-making.
End-to-end project delivery
Own and manage the full lifecycle of complex and cross-functional projects, ensuring delivery on time, within scope, and within budget.
Lead strategic initiatives such as market entries, platform enhancements, certifications, and product launches.
Coordinate dependencies and deliverables across multiple departments.
Strategic roadmap alignment
Partner with senior leadership and product teams to translate strategic objectives into structured project plans.
Support roadmap prioritization by assessing feasibility, risks, and business impact.
Ensure that project outcomes align with organizational targets and regulatory requirements.
Cross-functional leadership and stakeholder management
Lead and influence cross-department teams — including Product, Compliance, Legal, Marketing, Commercial, BI, and Engineering — facilitating effective collaboration and resolving conflicts across multi-team initiatives.
Mentor junior Project Managers and contribute to raising the maturity of the PM function.
Build and maintain strong relationships with senior leadership, external partners, vendors, and regulatory contacts, providing clear communication, alignment, and expectation-setting throughout the project lifecycle.
Manage project decisions and escalate critical issues when necessary.
Risk management and governance
Develop and maintain strategic risk frameworks to identify, assess, and mitigate project risks.
Lead risk workshops, implement contingency plans, and ensure compliance with internal governance processes.
Oversee change control procedures to maintain project stability during implementation.
Technical delivery oversight
Demonstrate strong technical understanding of the software development lifecycle (SDLC), integrations, technical architecture, and backend/frontend concepts.
Support technical teams by clarifying requirements, resolving blockers, and ensuring technical milestones are achieved.
Translate technical information into business language for stakeholders and executives.
Compliance and regulatory support
Collaborate with Compliance, Legal, and Risk teams to ensure alignment with iGaming regulatory standards for new markets and existing operations.
Support or lead regulatory-focused projects such as security audits, market certifications, or ISO initiatives.

s.h: Ensure documentation and procedures meet audit requirements.
s.t:
Reporting and communication
Prepare and deliver executive-level reporting, including progress updates, KPIs, identified risks, and recommendations.
Maintain full visibility of project status and ensure accurate documentation across PM tools and systems.
Provide structured reporting and presentations to senior management and steering committees.

Bachelor’s degree in IT, Project Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
Professional certification required: PRINCE2 Practitioner, PMP, Agile Certified Practitioner, or equivalent.
3–5+ years of proven project management experience, including at least 3 years working with software development teams or technical delivery environments.
2–3+ years of experience working in the iGaming industry or another highly regulated digital environment.
Strong understanding of Agile, Scrum, and Waterfall methodologies.
Advanced experience with Jira and other PM tools, including reporting and workflow configuration.
Experience leading cross-functional teams and managing high-complexity projects, with strong leadership, influencing, and decision-making skills.
Proficient in risk management, governance, and change control processes.
Excellent analytical abilities, problem-solving mindset, and data-driven decision making.
Strong documentation, reporting, and technical communication skills, with the ability to lead technical discussions and coordinate with engineers during design, development, and implementation phases.
Solid written and verbal communication skills in English.

Experience with regulatory, compliance, or market entry projects.

Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities.

A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

The International Rescue Committee helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future.

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC works with people forced to flee from war, conflict and disaster and the host communities that support them, as well as with those who remain within their homes and communities.

The IT department provides end-to-end solutions for the organization including application development & integration, system deployment, user experience and change management, quality assurance & testing, and overall Project Management in an effort to help the organization determine and implement the best solutions for its business needs.

This is a rare opportunity to sit at the center of one of the most consequential applications of AI in the social sector. As the IRC's AI Program Manager, you will help shape how a global humanitarian organization — operating in over 40 countries — harnesses artificial intelligence to improve outcomes for some of the world's most vulnerable people. This is not a role managing technology for its own sake; it is a role where smart, responsible AI adoption can directly accelerate impact at scale.
You will lead and coordinate the IRC's most important AI initiatives: driving enterprise AI projects from concept to delivery, ensuring that AI tools adopted across the organization are evaluated rigorously and responsibly, and coordinating the cross-functional teams working to embed AI into how the IRC operates. You will work at the intersection of technology, program delivery, and organizational change — partnering with senior leaders, technical experts, and frontline staff across the globe.
The right candidate is a fast-moving, proactive problem-solver who thrives in ambiguity, brings structure to complex and evolving landscapes, and is energized by the challenge of building something new in an environment where the stakes are high and the work is genuinely meaningful.
This role reports to the AI Governance and Transformation Lead, and works in close partnership with Director, IT Project and Portfolio Management, AI project leads, senior sponsors, and a broad community of practice across the organization.

AI Governance (60%)
The IRC is committed to adopting AI responsibly. As part of this, the organization has established a structured review process for AI use cases that carry potential high risks — whether related to data privacy, security, bias, or ethical considerations. As coordinator of this process, you will:
Manage the intake and documentation of AI use cases and tools flagged for high-risk review.
Assign cases to appropriate domain reviewers (e.g., legal, security, data protection, ethics) and coordinate their timely completion.
Maintain templates, trackers, and a full audit trail of all reviewed use cases and decisions.
Communicate clearly with requestors on process, status, and outcomes.
Draft and maintain guidance documentation, publishing decisions and resources to the IRC's internal staff portal.
Prepare agendas, materials, and logistics for review panel meetings.
Support the implementation of IRC’s enterprise AI policy, building out the necessary tools and processes in close collaboration with others.
Enterprise AI Project Management (40%)
Lead project management for high-priority, organization-wide AI initiatives. Responsibilities include:
Developing and maintaining detailed project plans, work breakdown structures, risk registers, and terms of reference.
Facilitating scrum, sprint planning, and retrospective meetings; driving delivery against milestones.
Designing and executing testing, rollout, and change management plans in partnership with cross-functional stakeholders.
Producing regular status reports for senior leadership, clearly communicating scope, progress, risks, and decisions.
Proactively surfacing and resolving blockers, issues, and risks before they become critical.

Maintains a productive working relationship with other project managers, business owners, AI project leads, senior sponsors of AI strategy initiatives, legal, security, and data protection teams, system users, and vendors.
Position Reports to: AI Governance and Transformation Lead
Position Reports in MIP to: Director, IT Project and Portfolio Management
Position directly supervises: N/A
Indirect Reporting: N/A

Headquarters & Global Offices Teams – multiple departments
Project Business Owners, business project team members outside IT, and wider stakeholders
Project Sponsor and Steering Committee members
Cross-functional AI management teams
AI Community of Practice (CoP) leads and members
Vendors and Consultants

6+ years of project management experience in IT or technology-driven environments.
Demonstrated success leading complex, multi-stakeholder programs with significant technology components.
Bachelor's degree required.
Experience with AI projects — whether in a project management, product, or operational capacity — strongly preferred.
Experience in international NGO or global humanitarian organizations preferred.
PMP, CSM, or equivalent project/program management certification preferred.

Agile & Program Management Demonstrated, hands-on experience with Agile methodologies — including Scrum, sprint planning, backlog management, and retrospectives — is required. Proficiency with project management tools such as Jira, Monday.com, or equivalents.
AI Literacy & Responsible AI Familiarity with AI concepts, use cases, and the compliance, security, data privacy, and ethical considerations that responsible AI adoption requires.
Communication & Executive Influence Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging from technical working teams through to senior executive leadership. Demonstrated ability to influence without authority — including managing up, keeping senior stakeholders aligned and accountable, and driving decisions in complex organizational environments.
Proactivity & Adaptability A self-starter who moves fast, takes initiative, and creates structure in ambiguous environments. Comfortable operating in a space that is still evolving — where processes are being built, priorities shift, and the ability to adapt quickly is essential.

Align stakeholders on roadmap, priorities, and measurable outcomes.
Lead cross-functional initiatives across time zones.

Cost per word/request
Throughput and latency
Enable data-driven decision-making for both technical and business stakeholders.

Narvar is growing! We are hiring a Technical Project Manager to drive our most complex, multi-team engineering initiatives — the ones with no single owning team, where progress depends on getting the sequencing right across groups that don't naturally coordinate with each other.
This is not a status-reporting role. You won't be writing production code, but you will build and maintain the real dependency graph behind a project: which team's output blocks which other team's start, where the critical path actually runs, and what has to happen in what order for the whole thing to land.

You'll follow technical discussions closely enough to spot those dependencies before they become blockers, and you'll proactively pull in the right people — across engineering, product, design, data, or leadership — before gaps turn into delays.

Dependency mapping and critical path management
Map cross-team dependencies for projects that span multiple engineering teams with no single owning team — identify what blocks what, and in what order work needs to happen
Maintain a live view of the critical path, not just individual teams' task lists, and flag when a slip in one team changes the achievable timeline for others
Surface hidden or emerging dependencies before they become blockers, particularly ones that no single team has visibility into because they sit at the seams between teams
Distill the graph into concise, honest updates for non-technical stakeholders and leadership — what's driving the timeline, what's at risk, and why
Cross-functional coordination
Identify when product management, design, data, legal, or other stakeholders need to be looped in — and act on it proactively, without waiting for engineers to flag it
Recognize when a dependency crosses team boundaries and make sure the teams on both sides of it are actually talking to each other, not just individually on track
Chase down answers, escalate when needed, and keep work moving forward
Serve as the connective tissue across engineering and adjacent functions throughout the delivery lifecycle — especially where no single team is positioned to see the whole picture
Technical context and decision support
Follow technical discussions closely enough to grasp the tradeoffs being made — architecture decisions, infrastructure choices, API design, build vs. buy — and understand how those choices ripple into other teams' work
Reason about sequencing implications of technical decisions: does this choice change what can be built in parallel versus what must be serial?
Surface implications of technical decisions for timeline, scope, or other teams
Know when a decision warrants broader input and facilitate getting it, without creating unnecessary process overhead
Documentation and operational hygiene
Keep the dependency graph, specs, decisions, and timelines documented and accessible
Ensure decisions made in Slack or ad-hoc meetings don't get lost, especially ones that affect teams beyond the room they were made in
Make it easy for anyone joining a project mid-stream to get up to speed quickly — including understanding why the sequencing is what it is

Systems and dependency thinking: You can look at multiple teams' plans and identify where they interlock — where a change in one ripples into another — even when no one team has full visibility into the whole
Technical fluency: You don't need to write code, but you need to follow engineering conversations comfortably — architecture diagrams, system tradeoffs, sprint planning — without hand-holding
Project management experience: 4+ years managing complex, multi-team software projects with several workstreams and stakeholders in a fast-moving environment — ideally including projects with no single owning team
Strong written communication: Able to distill a complex dependency picture into crisp, accurate updates for non-technical audiences
Proactive by default: You identify when to loop someone in without being asked, and you follow through without needing to be chased
Calm under ambiguity: Able to drive clarity and keep work moving without waiting for perfect information, a fully defined process, or a single team to own the outcome
Cross-functional credibility: Comfortable holding a room with engineers, product managers, designers, and executives — and earning trust from all of them

Prior experience as a software engineer, QA, or technical analyst
Familiarity with agile and scrum methodologies; experience with tools like Jira, Linear, or Shortcut, especially for modeling cross-team dependencies
Experience running programs (not just single-team projects) — i.e., initiatives coordinated across multiple teams toward a shared outcome
Experience working with distributed or remote engineering teams

The Agile Delivery Manager (ADM) is accountable for delivering business value across one or more agile teams, specifically in support of the organization’s digital transformation.

Acting as a servant leader and connector between strategic intent and operational execution, the ADM sits at the bridge point between the product/feature layer (Product Owners, Business Analysts, Business Owners) and the delivery layer (Engineering Managers, Developers, QA, and the Scrum Masters who own team-level performance).

The ADM ensures that delivery aligns with product roadmaps, value streams, and enterprise priorities.
This role is not about managing tasks—it’s about enabling flow, clarity, and measurable outcomes that advance the organization’s customer and business goals. The ADM owns the health and predictability of the Program Increment (PI): making sure it is planned well, tracked honestly, and delivered against — while escalating risks and dependencies before they become blockers. .

s.h: The role is responsible for the following results
s.t:
Delivery Flow and Value
Consistently leveraging lean and agile practices to achieve outcomes, not just complete output.
Orchestrate planning and coordination activities across multiple teams, including PI Planning, Scrum of Scrums and cross-team synchronization, and protecting the teams against interference and over commitment, to sustain focus and health velocity.
Advise Product Owners and Business Analysts in backlog management and sequencing to ensure clear cross-team prioritization.
Monitor flow and delivery health metrics (predictability, throughput, cycle time, PI objective achievement) and share them with teams to celebrate progress and surface improvement opportunities
Use performance and progress data to increase transparency and predictability in meeting commitments to the business.
Facilitate the adoption and evolution of agile practices to continuously improve how the organization produces high quality and high value outcomes.
Align teams with strategic goals through transparent sequencing of work, clear identification of cross-team dependencies; own the identification, tracking, and mitigation of delivery risks and issues, ensuring timely resolution or escalation.
Facilitate scaled/cross-team agile events (e.g., PI Planning, System Demo, Inspect & Adapt, Scrum of Scrums) so they are productive and time-boxed, setting a consistent standard of effectiveness across teams. Team-level ceremonies remain owned by Scrum Masters. Ensure delivery standards and definitions of done are applied consistently across the teams.
Enablement & Coaching
Coach Scrum Masters, Business Owners, Product Owners and Business Analysts to communicated in terms of value delivered rather than requirement fulfillment.
Guide continuous improvement through retrospectives, delivery health checks, and root-cause analysis at the multi-team and PI Levels
Build agile maturity through mentoring, modeling psychological safety, and reenforcing learning cycles.
Stakeholder Engagement
Translate delivery progress into business impact, reporting what value was realized, not just completed.
Own upward and outward communication of delivery status, risks, and PI outcomes to executives, business owners, the Governance & Transformation Lead, and technology leadership.
Ensure the “voice of delivery” is represented in strategic planning and portfolio discussions.

PI predictability (planned vs. delivered PI objectives) across teams in scope.
Flow metrics trend (cycle time, throughput, work-in-progress) shared and improving over time.
Time-to-resolution on escalated risks, issues, and cross-team dependencies.
Stakeholder-reported clarity and trust in delivery commitments (Business Owners, executive sponsors).
Team-reported psychological safety and agile maturity progression.

En tant que personne orientée vers les objectifs avec une expertise technique approfondie, vous supervisez le développement et la mise en œuvre de firmwares et logiciels dans un environnement réglementé pour des applications médicales ou industrielles.
